data._before_the_input: The class is resolved from the DEVICE, before the input narrows anything, because it answers a question about the listener's hardware and not about their cable. A converter with a direct DSD path still has one when it is reached over AirPlay; the transport is what cannot carry DSD, and the engine refuses the format for that reason, separately. So a resolved device may read dac_class direct_dsd_path beside native_dsd false: the first is the part, the second is the part through that input, and they are not in conflict.
data._derived_never_stored: NO RECORD CARRIES THIS FIELD, and none should. It is computed from fields already here - dsd_direct, dsd_reconverted_to_pcm, native_dsd, dop, internal_bypass, technology - so it cannot disagree with them and cannot be filled in by hand with a guess. A stored class would be a fifth place to get the same fact wrong. The engine writes it onto the resolved device and reads it nowhere: it is a label for a panel, not an input to a decision, and nothing in the cascade branches on it.
data._no_probe_establishes_it: A PROBE CAN NEVER SETTLE THIS. The class turns on dsd_direct, dsd_reconverted_to_pcm and internal_bypass, which are level-3 fields: no amount of asking a device what it accepts reveals what it does with it. So a zone whose device is known only from the driver resolves to undeclared however complete the probe is, and that is correct rather than a shortcoming. It is also the clearest statement of why the listener's answer is worth asking for.
data._not_an_architecture: READ THIS BEFORE THE NAMES MISLEAD YOU. These are not four architectures. The labels are architecture words and the definitions are PATH words: "NOS / R2R" means there is no oversampling to fight, or a filter that can be switched off - which is why an FPGA converter with a switchable stage belongs there and a resistor ladder with a DSD path does not. The axis is: how much of the device's own processing can be avoided, and with what. That is the only axis an upsampler needs.
data._order_is_data: The rules below are ORDERED and the order is the whole content of the classification, so it lives here rather than in code. The first rule that matches wins. The second rule - a direct DSD path outranks the architecture - is the one that decides the overlapping cases, and it is the source's own: "Some NOS / R2R DACs also provide a separate DSD conversion path, including models from Gustard, Holo Audio and the Denafrips Terminator range. If your DAC provides a dedicated DSD path, DSD is our recommended starting point." Without that line the ladders with a DSD path would match two classes and nothing would say which.
data._purpose: A single label for what a converter will DO to what it is sent, and by which format it can be got round. It exists for one job: to ask a listener who does not know their model a question they can answer. Today they are offered the chip families, and whether a converter is AKM or ROHM is not something a manual makes obvious; whether it is a ladder, a delta-sigma, a pure-DSD path or a PCM-only box is.
data._the_state_they_have_no_word_for: The last rule is not a default, it is an answer: a device that takes DSD whose path has NOT been established is path_unknown, not quietly sorted into one of the four. The source's four types assume the listener knows; this catalogue records dsd_direct as "to_be_measured" or "firmware_dependent" where nobody has checked, and that state has to survive the label rather than be rounded away. It is also why the class cannot replace the fields: it would erase the one distinction that makes the engine refuse to send DSD.

bypassable.label: NOS / R2R
bypassable.means: Nothing of the device's own stands between the stream and the analogue stage, or what does can be switched off. The output rate is then worth more than anything else, because reaching the rate at which the stage steps aside is the whole point.
bypassable.name: No oversampling, or a filter that can be turned off
bypassable.source: PGGB setup page, "Choose the closest type", read 2026-11-23, and its four cards. The vocabulary is theirs; the predicates below are ours, written against this catalogue's own fields. Their card: "NOS means non-oversampling; R2R refers to a resistor-ladder design. Choose this type if your DAC can play without oversampling or lets you turn its oversampling filter off."

direct_dsd_path.label: Pure 1-bit DSD
direct_dsd_path.means: DSD sent here goes past the device's own upsampling and modulation and reaches the analogue stage as it was computed. This is the one class where the modulator we choose is the modulator that converts.
direct_dsd_path.name: A direct DSD path to the analogue stage
direct_dsd_path.source: PGGB setup page, "Choose the closest type", read 2026-11-23, and its four cards. The vocabulary is theirs; the predicates below are ours, written against this catalogue's own fields. Their card: "These DACs have a direct 1-bit DSD conversion path. DSD input bypasses internal upsampling and modulation and goes directly to the analog conversion stage."

path_unknown.label: Not established
path_unknown.means: The device accepts DSD and nobody here has checked whether that path is direct. Not a default and not an absence of opinion: it is the answer, and it is why the engine does not send DSD on these.
path_unknown.name: Takes DSD, path not established
path_unknown.source: This catalogue. The source's own picker offers "I'm not sure yet" to the listener and has no type for a device whose path is unknown; this is that gap, named.

pcm_path.label: PCM DAC
pcm_path.means: Either the device takes no DSD at all, or it takes it and brings it back to PCM through its own filter. Sending DSD is work thrown away in the second case and impossible in the first.
pcm_path.name: PCM in, whatever is sent
pcm_path.source: PGGB setup page, "Choose the closest type", read 2026-11-23, and its four cards. The vocabulary is theirs; the predicates below are ours, written against this catalogue's own fields. Their card: "These DACs work best with PCM input. This group also includes DACs that accept DSD but convert it to PCM internally."

processed_path.label: Delta-sigma
processed_path.means: The device takes DSD and PCM and upsamples both internally. Some of that may be skipped at high rates, but there is no path without it. Nothing we send escapes the device's own stage.
processed_path.name: Always processed, whatever is sent
processed_path.source: PGGB setup page, "Choose the closest type", read 2026-11-23, and its four cards. The vocabulary is theirs; the predicates below are ours, written against this catalogue's own fields. Their card: "Delta-sigma DACs internally upsample both PCM and DSD input signals. Some processing may be skipped for high-rate PCM and DSD, but they do not provide a path without internal processing. ESS DACs are an example."

undeclared.label: Not identified
undeclared.means: No model record matched: the engine is working from the fallback, or from a maker and a chip family the listener declared. The conservative assumptions it then uses are NOT facts about a converter and must not be read back out as one — a fallback whose native_dsd is false because that is the careful branch would otherwise be announced as a PCM-only device, which nobody established.
undeclared.name: Nothing established about the hardware
undeclared.source: This catalogue's own fallback record. The source's picker shows the same state as "I'm not sure yet", beside its four types rather than among them.

predicates._why_this_block_exists: Three of the rules below test a PREDICATE, not a stored field, and until 2026-11-24 none of the three was defined anywhere. Measured on this catalogue's 27 records: a plausible alternative reading of `offered` moves FOUR records to a different class and empties `path_unknown` completely - which is exactly what _the_state_they_have_no_word_for says must never happen. Two of the three readings a reader could reasonably pick destroy the state this file insists on preserving. The order is published because the order is the content; the predicates have to be published for the same reason.

dsd_direct_offered._why_exactly_true: dsd_direct is a boolean_or_reason: true, false, or the NAME of the reason nobody knows yet. Reading a reason as an offer asserts a dedicated DSD path on the strength of nobody having checked. Measured: 5 of 27 records carry to_be_measured or firmware_dependent, 19%, and they are exactly the records whose class this predicate decides. Admitting them here is reading B, which empties path_unknown.
dsd_direct_offered.true: dsd_direct is exactly the boolean true.

internal_bypass_present._note: Presence is the whole test: a stated bypass rate is the claim. One record in 27 carries it.
internal_bypass_present.true: the internal_bypass key exists on the resolved device.

takes_dsd._the_defect_this_fixes: Rule 4 reads « no DSD by any path, so there is nothing to decide ». Until 2026-11-24 the predicate treated ABSENCE as a no, so the rule fired on records where nobody had said whether the device takes DSD at all. It fired twice on this catalogue and one of the two was wrong: schiit-yggdrasil carries native_dsd false and dop false, a stated no, and classified correctly; msb-diamond carried neither field and carried dsd_direct "to_be_measured", so the record said its DSD path was unmeasured while the class said there was none. This is the three-state rule the whole database rests on - no entry means nobody filled it in, "unknown" means the question was asked and closed - applied to a predicate that had quietly collapsed the first into the second.
takes_dsd.false: native_dsd AND dop are BOTH present AND both false. A stated no, on both transports.
takes_dsd.true: native_dsd is true, OR dop is true.
takes_dsd.unknown: either field is absent. Rule 4 then does NOT fire, and classification falls through to the rules below it.

rules.why: no model record matched: either the fallback, or a maker and a family the listener declared with no record behind them. In both the DSD fields are policy or absent, so no class may be derived from them
re-conversion is settled and decisive: whatever the architecture, DSD sent here comes back as PCM through a filter that is not ours
the source's own precedence: a dedicated DSD path outranks the architecture, which is what sorts a ladder that also converts DSD

no DSD by any path, native or DoP, so there is nothing to decide. REQUIRES A STATED NO on both transports - see predicates.takes_dsd. An absent field is not a no, and reading it as one classified a device whose DSD path was only unmeasured as PCM-only.
a stated bypass rate is the strongest form of "its own stage can be stepped out of the path", and it is stronger than a chip family

a ladder, whatever it does with DSD. Calling it delta-sigma would be false about the hardware, and high-rate PCM is the right starting point either way. Any doubt about its DSD path stays in dsd_direct, where it belongs
it takes DSD, it is not a ladder, and the path is stated NOT to be direct — which is exactly "no path without internal processing"
takes DSD, path not established, and no architecture settles it

data._not_a_field_count: A level here is NOT how many fields are filled. It is which decision the engine can make because of them. Counting fields produces a number nobody can act on; naming the decision tells a contributor exactly what their five minutes would unlock. The levels also differ by HOW the facts are obtained, which is what makes them a plan rather than a label: one level the machine discovers by itself, the next a person has to read, the last an instrument has to measure.
data._orthogonal_to_evidence: The level is completeness. It is NOT quality, and it never substitutes for the evidence rule: every field present, at every level, must have a source naming THAT device. A level-2 record with solid evidence is worth more than a level-3 record carrying a guessed chip family - the Gustard X30 was level 3 and simply wrong. A consumer's own documented/measured status answers a different question (how a fact was established) and the two compose: show both, conflate neither.
data._purpose: What a model record must carry to be worth adding, and what each further step buys. Written 2026-11-20, because the catalogue had no entry criterion at all and so could grow without anyone being able to say whether it was improving.
data._state_2026_11_23: Measured across the 27 records on 2026-11-23 by replaying the engine over each one, with the cascade taken into account: 19 are complete at level 2 and 3 carry a USB identity, so the catalogue is essentially a level-2 catalogue. ZERO are complete at level 3, and the shortfall is concentrated exactly where documentation runs out - the real ladder depth is known for 7 records, an internal bypass for 1, the PCM/DSD offset for 16, and whether DSD is re-converted for 15. That distribution is the argument for the levels: the cheap half is nearly done and the expensive half has barely started, and a single completeness percentage would have hidden both facts. CORRECTED: the 2026-11-20 figure read 24 at level 2, because that count did not apply this file's own field list - it left out `inputs`, which 6 records do not carry. The four field counts were right. A self-description that does not run its own criterion is the one number nobody re-checks.
data._state_2026_11_24: Measured on 2026-11-24 against this file's own field list: 17 of the 27 records are complete at level 2, down from 19, and 9 carry no input block. THE HISTORY OF THIS NUMBER, because it has been wrong twice: 24 until 2026-11-20 (a count that did not run this file's own criterion), 19 until 2026-11-24, 17 today. The drop is not a loss of knowledge. Two rounds of withdrawal happened, and both were decided field by field against each record's own quoted source rather than by analogy: first the per-input ceilings of chord-generique, ifi-generique and merging-hapi, which were one model's asserted under a brand catch-all or under a modular unit; then the DEVICE-level ceilings of ifi-generique and msb-diamond, whose quotes carry no figure at all - MSB's entire evidence is the sentence « it is an R2R DAC (and thus native PCM) », which names no rate. TWO RECORDS WERE EXAMINED AND KEPT, which is why this says so: chord-generique's quote names both the rate and the brand (« passing 705.6/768k PCM to a Chord DAC »), so its pcm_max_hz is supported where iFi's and MSB's were not; and merging-hapi's figures are true of one Hapi, its defect being the SUBJECT - one record for every generation and fitted card - which is an identity question, not a withdrawal. Checking each field instead of removing for symmetry changed the answer: three records were announced for withdrawal and two were withdrawn. FIVE of the nine records with no input block still have no written reason that mentions inputs: akm-generique, ess-generique, mola-mola-generique, smsl-d6, unknown. The first was a list of four; smsl-d6 was missing from it because the check looked for the PRESENCE of a gloss instead of reading what the gloss said - its doubt discusses a chip family and never its inputs. They are catch-alls, which is probably legitimate, and probably is not evidence. A counted hole, not a tidy one.
data._why_partial_records_are_safe: An incomplete record can never make Auto worse than no record, because of how the cascade resolves: a field the record omits is inherited from the brand or the chip family, and a field nobody knows is "unknown", which makes the engine take the conservative branch. The danger is never missing data. It is data that is present and wrong, which is why the entry gate below is about evidence and identity rather than about filling boxes.

levels._an_identity_can_be_generic: An identity does not always name a model, and a match must therefore say what it resolves TO. In this database `ta-dac200` carries one USB identity (0x1852/0x5034) across four products - DAC 200, HA 200, SDV 3100 HV, DAC8 DSD - and `mola-mola-generique` carries a VID/PID with `model: unknown`. A VID/PID can thus establish a range, or only a brand. That is why `device_match` names the subject it resolves to and the level it establishes, instead of assuming a device.
levels._gate: A record at this level is admissible with EITHER an exact USB identity OR a resolved match (`device_match`) carrying its own evidence. With neither it resolves identically to the brand catch-all that already exists, so it is a duplicate row carrying no fact - and a row that looks like knowledge without being any is worse than an honest gap. With one of the two it earns its place, because it is what turns an unidentified device into a named one.
levels._relaxed_2026_11_24: The gate first asked for a USB identity and nothing else. That excluded every device the field can actually report: a player asks the network, and a UPnP announcement carries no USB descriptor at all. Worse, the announcement does not identify the hardware - it names the renderer software. One announced string routinely covers many different converters (upmpdcli, a Diretta bridge, or any player that announces itself all do this), and the brand announced is very often not the brand of the device. Both are verifiable by anyone on any UPnP network; the proportions were measured on a production export on 2026-11-24 and are recorded OUTSIDE this repository, with the editor's data. So the resolution is a claim like any other: it carries evidence, it can be contested, and it is NEVER inferred from the announced string alone.
levels.name: Identified
levels.obtained_from: A USB descriptor, where the chain is USB: free, and exact. Otherwise a PERSON. What a network player announces of itself over UPnP names the RENDERER - the software serving the stream - and not the converter behind it, so turning an announcement into a device is a human act and is recorded as one.
levels.unlocks: The converter is recognised by name instead of being an unknown device, and resolves to its brand. Nothing else changes: it behaves exactly as the brand's catch-all.

levels._this_is_the_target: Level 2 is where a record should normally enter, because it costs a contributor nothing and it is where the engine stops guessing.
levels.name: Basic - what the device accepts
levels.obtained_from: THE PROBE GIVES THIS FOR FREE. Any player already asks a device what rates and formats it accepts; the contribution form carries the answer. Per-input ceilings are also the one thing makers reliably publish.
levels.unlocks: The whole PCM path, correctly: the rate ladder stops falling back to a conservative 192 kHz, the right ceiling applies per input, and DSD transport is known. This is the level the PCM-only Auto mode needs, and it needs nothing beyond it.

levels._the_hard_part: Makers publish the chip and the accepted formats. They do not publish the PCM/DSD level offset, whether DSD is re-converted internally, or a ladder's real depth as opposed to its interface's. Those four fields are why this level is slow, and browsing maker sites will not supply them.
levels.name: Advanced - what the device does inside
levels.obtained_from: A datasheet, a maker's answer, or the reference implementation author's replies. NEVER a probe: no amount of asking a device what it accepts reveals what it does with it. This is the level that needs a person.
levels.unlocks: The DSD path: whether to send DSD at all, which modulator order, the level compensation so switching format does not change the volume, the real ladder depth to quantise to, and any rate at which the device steps its own processing aside.

levels._state: No record in this catalogue is at this level, and none will be without hardware.
levels.name: Measured
levels.obtained_from: Laboratory measurement of that device. This is the same thing a vendor catalogue means by "measured", so the two statuses are the same axis and should be one field, not two.
levels.unlocks: A per-device correction profile, and confirmation of the level-3 fields that were taken from documentation.

data._cost: Author: "DAC correction can increase the load to 1.3x - 2x".
data._for_us: We cannot build correction profiles - that needs lab measurement of each device. But the architecture should leave room for one, applied last, at the output rate. And the precondition is a field we already carry: a device that is not bit-exact cannot be corrected, which is one more reason to know that property.
_preconditions: The device must be close to bit-perfect (direct DSD or NOS PCM).
A separate profile is needed per output rate, and per device setting that affects the output.
Built from a large number of analog-output measurements, iteratively. Time-consuming per DAC.
data._source: Interview with the author, Audiophile Style, 2026-11-11.
data._what: Correction of the errors introduced by the DAC's mixed-domain conversion stage and by its analog stages - I/V, reconstruction filter, line driver. Not the digital stage.
data._who_benefits: "Better ones usually benefit more. So it is really more about improving DACs further, rather than fixing a bad one."
data._why_not_in_the_dac: Requires heavy DSP at the output rate, in the MHz range, and the DAC chip has no knowledge of the analog sections that follow it.

data._entry_criterion: A model record is admissible when it meets BOTH of these, and no number of filled fields substitutes for either. ONE: every field it states has a source naming that device - the rule validate.py enforces, and the one the Gustard records failed for months while looking complete. TWO: it carries either a USB identity or at least one fact its brand does not already supply. A record that states nothing its brand has not already stated, and cannot be matched automatically, is a row that adds a name to a list and knowledge to nothing. See _completeness for what each further level buys and who has to do the work.
data._the_ess_exception: ESS is the one family that fixes dsd_direct, at false, for every device: the chip leaves makers no choice, since everything passes through its internal DSP in PCM and DSD alike. Hence correctable = false across the family - a correction cannot travel through variable processing we do not control. It does NOT fix dsd_reconverted_to_pcm, which the family sets to false: the author recommends DSD output to ESS parts by name, and a fifth-order modulator before the ES9039. The exception is about correctability, and nothing else.
data._the_field_that_fools_people: Two fields here look like one, and until 2026-11-20 they were one. dsd_direct asks whether the stream reaches conversion unfiltered, which governs correctable. dsd_reconverted_to_pcm asks whether the device undoes our work, which governs whether Auto sends DSD at all. The Denafrips evidence establishes the second ("it doesn't do bit-perfect DSD conversion, but instead runs some kind of PCM conversion"); the ESS family note establishes only the first. Merging them silenced DSD on every ESS device and made the order-5 modulator rule unreachable - dead code found by reading the catalogue against itself. Neither field is a property of the chip, with the one exception below. The six AKM records here carry three different dsd_direct values. Never infer either from the chip: measure, or cite a documented answer about that device. This is why source is required on every record.
data._unknown: Every field in this catalogue has three possible states and they must stay distinguishable. A VALUE means known at this level. ABSENT means this level says nothing, so the level above decides - model, then brand, then chip family, then the global default. The string "unknown" means this level has looked and there is no answer: a finished state, not a blank, and the engine takes the conservative branch instead of substituting a default. null is gone from the catalogue and forbidden by the schema. It used to carry both "nobody filled this in" and "nobody knows", which are opposite facts about where to spend effort, and in one record it silently erased a chip family's bit depth. That is a better answer than the escape hatch written the morning after the defect was reported.
data._what_the_chip_fixes: Three fields, and only three, are properties of the silicon and are therefore safe to inherit from the family without ever checking the device: modulator_order, pcm_dsd_level_offset_db, and shaper_linearization. They do not vary between two devices built on the same chip, and a record that restates them is restating the family.
data._what_the_implementation_fixes: Everything else belongs to the device, not to the chip: pcm_max_hz, dsd_max, native_dsd, dop, analog_filter. These are decided by the USB receiver, the firmware and the output stage. The four ESS records in this file make the point - 384 kHz on exaSound and Merging against 768 on Topping, DSD256 against DSD512, and a good analog stage on the NADAC where the others are simple. Same chip, four different sets of numbers.
data._where_the_family_is_too_coarse: ess_sabre does not distinguish an ES9018 from an ES9038PRO. The family's three assertions hold across the Sabre line with one soft spot: switching_elements = single, which is what yields a 5th order modulator. A device paralleling eight ES9038PRO channels is arguably multi-element, hence 7th order. The catalogue follows the source, which states the rule at brand level. If such a device turns up, this is exactly what a device record is for: a record overrides its family field by field, and the override needs its own evidence.
data.analog_filter: Quality of the analog reconstruction stage: switchable, good, simple, weak. Feeds the modulator order decision - order 5 suits simple stages, order 7 demands a good filter.
data.brand: The maker, as a key into brands.json. "unknown" where no brand is known, which is the state of the two chip-family fallbacks. Separating the brand from the model is what keeps the listener's first list short and what lets a fact true of a whole range be written once.
data.chip: What the conversion stage actually is, in words. A part number where there is one, a count where there are several, or the maker's own design named as such. It is DOCUMENTATION, not a dispatch key: the engine reads family and technology and never this. It exists so that a converter built by its maker can be described precisely without inventing a family that would carry no defaults - see chips.json _a_makers_own_converter.
data.correctable: Whether a per-device correction profile could ever apply. Precondition stated by the author: a DAC too far from bit-perfect performs varying internal DSP that does not let the correction reach the conversion stage consistently. In practice corrections exist only for devices doing direct DSD or NOS PCM. See _device_correction.
data.device_settings: Settings to make on the device itself, not in the module.
data.dsd_direct: Does the DSD stream reach the conversion stage without passing through an internal filter? This field decides ONE thing and one only: whether a per-device correction could ever apply, i.e. correctable. It does NOT decide whether Auto sends DSD - that is dsd_reconverted_to_pcm, and conflating the two is the mistake this catalogue made until 2026-11-20. Values: true, false, firmware_dependent, to_be_measured. Beware of vocabulary: some manufacturers confuse "DSD Direct" with "Native DSD". The latter only describes the transport. Only measurement settles it.
data.dsd_reconverted_to_pcm: Does the device bring DSD back to PCM internally before converting? Decisive, and the only field that makes Auto send PCM to a DSD-capable device: a converter that re-converts has nothing to gain from receiving DSD, because it would redo - worse - the work we have just done. true, false, or null when no evidence settles it. null is permissive: with no evidence of re-conversion, Auto sends DSD. Requires evidence in source, exactly like dsd_direct, and is never inferred from it: a device can fail to be bit-exact (dsd_direct false) and still convert the DSD it is given, which is the ESS case.
data.internal_bypass: Some converters stop processing the signal themselves once the incoming rate is high enough: feed them above a threshold and their own interpolation stage is out of the path. That is worth more than the rate itself, because it removes a stage we do not control and cannot correct for. Fields: format, at_or_above_hz, bypasses (what stops, in words), strength ("prefer" raises the candidate's score, "require" makes it a floor), and source. The engine reports it in the trace, so a listener fed 705.6 kHz on a converter that accepts 768 learns why. Not a quirk of one maker: the pattern recurs wherever a device has an internal filter it will step aside from.
data.model: The model alone, without the maker's name: "May", not "Holo Audio May". The value "unknown" marks the brand's CATCH-ALL record - what Auto resolves when the listener knows who made their converter but not which one, and what the model list's own "I don't know" entry selects. Five records here are catch-alls, and before the split they were hiding inside the name field as "Chord (Qutest, Hugo, Dave)" or "Denafrips (Ares / Pontus / Venus / Terminator)" - brand-level assertions wearing the shape of a device.
data.provenance: Which inlet a fact came through - probe, maker, listener or agent - as distinct from source, which is the citation itself. Two different questions: source says what was read, provenance says how much to trust it and who to go back to. Recorded per field group rather than per record, since one record routinely mixes a probe's ceilings with a forum answer about its internals. See _governance.
data.technology: What the conversion stage is: delta_sigma, r2r, discrete_dsd or fpga. This is what the ENGINE dispatches on - it decides whether a shaper can linearise the stage - while family is a bundle of defaults. A record needs no family and can state every field itself; it resolves perfectly and the engine never notices. But a record without a family MUST state technology, because the fallback is delta_sigma: right for most converters, wrong for every resistor ladder and every discrete DSD stage, and until 2026-11-20 applied silently. validate.py now refuses the combination of no family and no technology.
data.usb: USB identity, the key automatic identification matches on. vid and pid are the USB vendor and product identifiers as integers; product_strings are the manufacturer and product strings the device declares, lowercased and stripped. NEVER guess these: an identity filled from memory makes the engine assert a technology, a modulator order and a level offset for the wrong device, and a wrong record is worse than no record. Fill them from the device itself, or from the Linux kernel USB audio quirk tables. A record with a null vid is still usable by name — it simply never matches automatically.

data._facts_expire: A fact can be true and then stop being true, and this catalogue already holds the proof: a Gustard record says DSD Direct works 'now' because the maker shipped new firmware. So a level-3 fact may be bound to a firmware version, and the field value firmware_dependent already exists for the case where it varies. Any automated watching should treat a firmware release on a device in the catalogue as a reason to re-ask, not as noise.
data._four_inlets: Facts arrive by four different doors and the doors are not equally reliable, so the record stores WHICH DOOR a fact came through - the provenance - as well as the citation itself. Today a record says where a value was read; it does not say how it got in, and after a year of automated collection that is the difference between a catalogue and a pile.
data._precedence: When two inlets disagree about one field, in order: a laboratory measurement; the device itself for what it accepts; the maker in writing for what it does; a documented answer from a recognised expert; the maker's published sheet; a review or retailer listing; a forum post; an agent's inference, which never wins anything because it never writes. Where the order does not settle it, NEITHER value is written: the conflict goes into _verify with both sides named, and the field stays unknown. That is what the Gustard X30 should have had for months - an unsourced AKM filing against the kernel's own ESS comment - and silence let the wrong one stand.
data._who_administers: One maintainer owns the schema, arbitrates conflicts and publishes. Makers write their own devices' level-3 fields under their own name. Listeners submit. Agents propose. NOBODY writes anonymously: every field carries who asserted it and through which inlet, because a catalogue whose value is evidence cannot have a row nobody is accountable for.

inlets._carried_by: The contribution form, filled automatically before the listener sees it.
inlets.name: The device itself, probed
inlets.trust: Highest for what it covers, and SILENT beyond it. It reports what the device DID, not what a sheet claims, which is why it outranks the maker's own specification for these fields. It can say nothing at all about level 3.
inlets.writes: Levels 1 and 2 only: the USB identity, and what the device accepts per input.

inlets._no_answer_is_a_state: A maker asked and silent must be recorded as asked-and-silent, with the date. Otherwise the same question is sent every quarter and the absence of an answer never becomes information.
inlets._the_incentive: A maker who fills their own records gets their devices set up correctly by every installation that reads this database, named properly in the panel, and reachable by automatic identification. That is a real return for an afternoon's work, and it should be how they are approached: not a favour asked, but a listing improved. It also gives the one thing no scrape can: an attributable answer from the party that knows.
inlets.name: The manufacturer, in writing and identified
inlets.trust: High for level 3, and WEAKER THAN THE PROBE for level 2 - a published sheet often states the chip's capability rather than the implementation's. The inversion is the point: ask the device what it accepts, ask the maker what it does.
inlets.writes: Level 3 above all: the chip, the internal behaviour, the level offset, any bypass rate. Exactly what no probe can reach.

inlets._never_overwritten: A listener's correction of their own device is never re-asserted over by a record. It is the one case where the person in the room knows more than the catalogue.
inlets.name: A listener, through the panel
inlets.trust: Variable, and it does not matter much, because what the listener supplies that nobody else can is the MODEL NAME for a USB identity. The probe attached to their submission carries the facts.
inlets.writes: A new device, a correction to an existing one, or a model name for an identity the catalogue sees but cannot name.

inlets._what_it_is_good_at: Watching: a firmware release that changes a device's behaviour, a new model from a brand already in the catalogue, a measurement index growing, a maker's sheet changing under a URL already cited. Noticing change is worth more than first collection, because nobody re-reads a page they already read.
inlets.name: An automated agent reading forums, sheets and measurement indexes
inlets.trust: Lowest, and the restriction is not about accuracy - today's pass over five manufacturer sites was accurate. It is that this catalogue's whole value is that every field is attributable, and an unattended writer destroys that faster than it fills anything. An agent's finding enters as a proposal carrying its URL, its date and the exact sentence it read, and a human accepts it.

data._never: No fuzzy or partial matching. Match with certainty or not at all. A vendor id never selects a device record, and the vendor ids under not_identifying never select anything.
_order: exact match on usb.vid and usb.pid -> that device record
exact match on a normalised product_string -> that device record
match on usb.vid alone, against _identification.vendors.by_vid, and only where that entry carries a family -> that family, never a device record
no match: the device is named from its descriptor string and resolved as unknown
data._state: Filled 2026-11-19 from the Linux kernel USB audio quirk tables. Three records carry an exact vid:pid; nine vendor identifiers are recorded, of which four carry a family; two vendor identifiers are recorded as non-identifying so that nobody later reads a brand into them. The remaining twenty-four records carry no USB identity: the kernel does not name them, because a device only enters those tables when it needs a workaround. Holo, Denafrips, Chord, Topping, exaSound, Bricasti, LAiV and Merging are absent for that reason, not because they are unidentifiable - their identities have to come from the devices themselves. No product_string is filled: the kernel tables carry comments written by patch authors, not the strings the devices declare.

vendors._purpose: USB vendor identifiers the kernel names. A vendor id says which house built the device, never which model. It may only be used to pick a family, and only where family is filled below. It must never be used to select a device record: the same vendor ships devices whose bits, maxima and DSD behaviour differ.

by_vid.note: Accuphase builds its own MDS converter across the range; the family holds.
T+A's own discrete converter across the current range.
Every MSB converter is a ladder. The model, and therefore the bit depth and the maxima, is not knowable from the vendor id.
Second MSB identifier, on the older USB module. The comment names no model.
No family: Gustard ships ESS and AKM in the same range. The kernel comment says "Ess based" but the A26 and the X30 are AKM.
No family: the Yggdrasil is a ladder, the small Schiit devices are delta-sigma. The only Schiit the kernel names is the Hel, which is not in this file.

by_vid.cite: quirks.c USB_ID(0x2a39, 0x3f8c) and 0x3fa0 /* RME Digiface USB */
by_vid.note: No family: the only RME the kernel names is the Digiface, an interface and not a converter. The ADI-2 carries no entry.
No family: one vendor id for two brands and for devices ranging from a CD player to a headphone amplifier.
No family and no brand: this identifier is shared between makers. Only the full vid:pid pair means anything here.

not_identifying.cite: quirks.c VENDOR_FLG(0x152a, /* Thesycon devices */) and DEVICE_FLG(0x152a, 0x85dd, /* SMSL USB DAC */)
not_identifying.note: A USB audio driver house, not a converter maker. SMSL, Topping, Gustard and many others ship under it. Even 0x152a:0x85dd, which the kernel labels "SMSL USB DAC", names no model. Never infer a brand, a family or a record from this vendor id.

not_identifying.cite: quirks.c VENDOR_FLG(0x20b1, /* XMOS based devices */) and DEVICE_FLG(0x20b1, 0x2009, /* XMOS Ltd DIYINHK USB Audio 2.0 */)
not_identifying.note: The USB receiver chip's vendor id, carried by a large part of the market, Chord and iFi among them. A single pid under it can mean a model - 0x3089 is the Mola Mola - but the vendor id alone means nothing. Never infer a brand, a family or a record from it.

data: Five makers checked independently on 2026-11-20 - Chord, T+A, Gustard, Topping and Denafrips - and all five say the same thing: USB and I2S carry the device's full capability, while the whole S/PDIF family (coaxial, optical, AES/EBU) stops at 24-bit/192 kHz and carries DSD only over DoP, to DSD64. The DoP figure is not an extra fact: 192 kHz divided by 16 IS DSD64, which is what the engine derives, so the makers and the arithmetic agree without consulting each other. The one exception found is Chord's BNC coaxial at 384 kHz. This regularity is RECORDED, not generalised: devices whose sheets were not found carry no input block rather than an assumed one, because a pattern across five devices is a good reason to go and look and a bad reason to stop looking.

data._one_to_many_in_both_directions: One announced string resolves to many devices (the bridge case above). One device also announces many strings, because spelling varies by firmware and by protocol. So a match is never a column on either side: it is a row, like every other assertion here.
data._resolves_at_is_not_a_detail: An identity is frequently generic. In this database `ta-dac200` carries one USB identity (0x1852/0x5034) across four products - DAC 200, HA 200, SDV 3100 HV, DAC8 DSD - and `mola-mola-generique` carries a VID/PID whose `model` is "unknown". A match that claimed a device where the evidence establishes a range would assert a chip, a modulator order and a level offset for the wrong product. Hence the field, and hence `unknown` rather than a guess.
data._the_oui_names_the_board: An OUI is far more reliable than a name, and still not a brand. The Raspberry Pi Foundation's ranges answer for a whole shelf of streamers built on that board, so the OUI gives the maker of the NETWORK CARD, which for those products is not the audio brand. Useful as corroboration, never alone - which is what `confidence: oui_only` says.
data._the_rule: WHAT A SYSTEM REPORTS IS NEVER THE IDENTITY. The identity is this database's own frozen slug. Everything a driver, a player or a network announces is matched TO it, from the outside.
data._what: How something reported by another system is attached to a subject of this database. A match is an ASSERTION, not a key: it carries evidence, it can be contested, and withdrawing a wrong one touches no fact about any device.
data._why_this_exists: Because the announcement does not name the device. Over UPnP a player announces the RENDERER - the software serving the stream - so a bridge or daemon running in front of a converter announces itself, not the converter. One announced string therefore covers many different devices, and the brand announced is frequently not the brand of the hardware. Anyone can verify this on any UPnP network; it was measured on a production export on 2026-11-24, and the proportions are held outside this repository with that editor's data.
data._withdrawing_one: Delete the row. No fact moves, no record changes, and the device keeps every assertion it had. That is the whole reason a match is not a field on the device.

fields.announced_brand: The manufacturer string as reported, kept verbatim. Never cleaned: the raw form is the evidence.
fields.announced_model: The model string as reported, verbatim.
fields.confidence: How the match was established, not a score: exact_usb_identity | human_resolved | announced_string | oui_only. The weakest two never stand alone.
fields.oui: The first three bytes of the MAC, upper case, AA:BB:CC - and never more. Three bytes name the maker; the other three name one person's machine and are not ours. Truncate on RECEIPT, not on display: a value never written cannot leak.
fields.resolves_at: brand | range | device. What the match actually establishes, which is often less than a model.
fields.resolves_to: The subject's slug in this database.
fields.source: The evidence, quoted, as for any assertion.
fields.system: Which outside system reported it - a player, a driver, a catalogue. Named, because a string means different things in different systems.

data._asking_beats_reading: Manufacturers are the one party with an active interest in these records being right, and they are the only party that can answer the questions that matter. A maker who fills in their own level-3 fields - whether the DSD path is direct, whether DSD is re-converted internally, the real depth of the ladder, the PCM/DSD level offset - gives in one email what no amount of reading gives at all. Measured on the candidate sources below: they reach level 1 and a PARTIAL level 2, and carry dsd_reconverted_to_pcm and dsd_direct for nobody. Scraping a maker's site is legitimate and useful, and it is still the cheap half of the problem.
data._citing_proves_it_does_not_licence_it: READ THIS BEFORE ASSUMING ATTRIBUTION SETTLES ANYTHING. Naming the source does not create permission that was never granted. Attribution is a CONDITION of some licences, not a substitute for one: it satisfies CC BY where CC BY applies, and changes nothing where no licence was given. The citation is mandatory here for a different reason, and a good one - it is this catalogue's evidence rule, no claim without a quoted source, which makes a fact checkable and refutable by the next person. That is worth everything and it is not a right to take.
data._how_to_read_a_makers_site: Read robots.txt and the site's terms of use first: a site's terms are a CONTRACTUAL layer that exists whatever the law says about facts, and plenty of them forbid automated extraction. A robots.txt returning 404 is not a prohibition, and not a permission either - it is silence. Prefer the manual or the datasheet PDF: those are published precisely to be read and quoted. Take the fields a record needs, device by device, never the whole catalogue. Rate-limit, and identify the client by a generic name - never by a person's contact details. Record the URL and THE DATE THAT SOURCE WAS READ, per fact: a maker's specification changes with firmware revisions, so a fact without its own date cannot be re-checked. For a bulk take from a named manufacturer, the decision is the project owner's, not a contributor's: it is their exposure.
data._permission_alone_is_not_enough: A yes is not a licence. ODAC republishes its data under CC BY-SA 4.0, so anything taken in bulk must be redistributable UNDER THAT, by whoever we got it from. Which rules out more than people expect: CC0, CC BY and CC BY-SA are compatible and carry attribution forward. CC BY-NC is NOT - this catalogue allows commercial use, that is the point of the licence choice. CC BY-ND is NOT, since the data is reshaped on the way in. ODbL is not straightforwardly compatible with an outgoing CC BY-SA and needs advice before it is assumed to be. And an informal permission - an email saying go ahead - usually grants USE and says nothing about onward redistribution under a share-alike licence, which is the only thing we actually need. So the thing to obtain, and to record with the data, is permission to redistribute under CC BY-SA 4.0 with attribution. Anything less is a fact-by-fact source, like all the others.
data._status: WHAT HAS BEEN TAKEN FROM THESE SOURCES: nothing. Not one field in this catalogue comes from any of them. They are candidates, listed 2026-11-20, each with the column it could actually fill - because breadth is not the question. The question is which column a source can fill, and on what terms we may pass it on.
data._the_field_none_of_them_has: None of these carries dsd_reconverted_to_pcm or dsd_direct - the two fields that decide whether a consumer sends DSD at all. They come from measurement or from a documented statement about that device, and nothing else. So these sources can carry the catalogue from level 0 to level 1 at scale, and to a PARTIAL level 2. Never to a complete one.
data._the_gap_in_this_file: Measured 2026-11-24: this file lists five candidate sources and records the licence of NONE of them. It reasons about redistribution in the abstract while never stating, per source, what the terms are - which is the one thing that decides whether case TWO or case THREE applies. Every candidate below now carries a `licence` field set to "not established", because that is what is true. It is not filled in with a guess: a licence invented from memory is exactly the kind of fact this catalogue refuses everywhere else, and it would be invented about somebody else's legal position.
data._the_makers_own_pages: THE FOURTH CASE, and the widest one: a manufacturer publishing specifications for its OWN products. This is not a compilation of other people's facts - it is the maker stating facts about hardware it built, on a page it chose to publish. Recording that a given converter accepts 768 kHz over USB, from the maker's own page, is using a fact, and a fact is not protectable. The sui generis right protects the ASSEMBLY of a database, not the facts inside it, so a maker's product page sits in case ONE and not case TWO. IT IS THE EXTENT THAT DECIDES, NOT THE METHOD. Reading a page by hand and reading it with a script are the same act on the same fact. What changes the act is taking a SUBSTANTIAL PART of a collection: a maker's full product catalogue can itself be a database with substantial investment behind it, and mirroring the whole of it is a different thing from looking up the device a contributor actually owns. One fact per device, because someone needed that device, is the shape that stays in case one - and it is the shape every record here already has.
data._three_cases_not_two: LOOKING SOMETHING UP IS NOT THE SAME ACT AS REPUBLISHING A LIST, and there is a third case that the first two hide. ONE: a fact. Reading a public page and recording that a given converter uses a given chip is using a fact, and facts are not protectable. This is what every record here does, one device at a time, with the source named. It needs nobody's permission. TWO: a compilation, taken wholesale. Copying a compiled list into this catalogue and then passing that catalogue on is a different act. A compiled database can be protected in its own right - the European sui generis database right - independently of whether any single fact in it is. Not done, and not to be done. THREE: a compilation we are ALLOWED to take. This is the only door to bulk import, and it is the case worth working on rather than working around. It is also why 'licence to be settled first' on a source below is an invitation to ASK, not a verdict.

All five makers above put optical at 192 kHz, and interfaces.json still assumes 96 for a device that has not said. That is deliberate. The failure modes are not symmetric: assuming 96 on a 192-capable input costs the listener one rate step they will never notice, while assuming 192 on a 96-capable one costs a device that does not lock and a zone that plays nothing. Five devices in one class is also a thin basis for a default that must hold for every device nobody has checked. The right fix is not a braver default - it is filling the per-device values, which is what the block above does.

open_doubt.device_level_resolution: The DEVICE-level ceilings went the same way as the per-input ones, and for a reason that needs no judgement: this claim's quoted source carries NO figure at all - it reads « All iFi DACs that support DSD and are using TI/BB chipset » and « TI/BB DAC chips only support bit-perfect DSD playback ». It supports a chip family and a DSD behaviour, and nothing about a rate. The figures it was carrying (768 kHz, DSD512) were the Pro iDSD's, as the withdrawn per-input claim said in its own words. Withdrawing the per-input ceilings and keeping the device-level ones would have left the record LOOKING reviewed while still asserting one model's rates for the range.
evidence_kept: iFi Pro iDSD manual, read 2026-11-20, which states it plainly: « Inputs other than USB are currently limited to maximum sample rates of 192kHz PCM and DSD64 via DoP », against USB at 768 kHz and DSD1024.
open_doubt.resolution: The per-input ceilings were WITHDRAWN on 2026-11-24, on the claim's own confession: its source ended with « This record is the range's catch-all and the figures are the Pro iDSD's; the Neo and micro models were not documented per input. » A source that says it does not cover the subject is evidence against the claim it carries.
open_doubt.text: The family here is read from a conditional sentence: "All iFi DACs that support DSD and are using TI/BB chipset" describes the ones that use that silicon rather than claiming the range does. This record is the brand's catch-all, so it asserts the chip for every iFi converter on evidence that does not go that far.
open_doubt.what_would_resolve_it: A per-model record (ifi/pro-idsd) carrying them. The quoted sentence is unusually clean evidence and should not be lost on the way.

Chip-level facts only. » Its identity says the same - brand "unknown", model "unknown" - and it shares that identity exactly with ess-generique/akm-generique and with the `unknown` catch-all. Three device records, one identity, coexisting only because the real key is the slug. THE DOUBT IS WHETHER IT SHOULD BE A DEVICE AT ALL: what it carries are AKM's chip-level defaults, and database/chip-families/akm.json is where those live.
open_doubt.what_would_resolve_it: Move what is left to database/chip-families/akm.json, which already holds this silicon's real properties, and delete the device record. Deferred to the identity pass, because it is the same question as the brand catch-alls, the typed aliases and the missing range level - and that pass should happen once.
open_doubt.why_withdrawn: These four fields are the ones this catalogue's own vocabulary says a chip does NOT fix. `_what_the_implementation_fixes` reads: « Everything else belongs to the device, not to the chip: pcm_max_hz, dsd_max, native_dsd, dop, analog_filter. These are decided by the USB receiver, the firmware and the output stage. » A record that declares itself not a measured device was therefore asserting, for every converter built on this silicon, precisely the four values the silicon does not determine. The chip family deliberately carries none of them, so nothing is lost by removing them: they were not a duplicate of the family, they were an invention on top of it. Same defect withdrawn from ifi-generique and msb-diamond earlier today; leaving it standing on the two WIDEST subjects in the database would have made that pass inconsistent.
